subject: Offset request for delayed tooling integration — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Lexi Turner <lexi@omnipay.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@omnipay.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Delay on tooling integration — request for offset

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the last demo. I wanted to flag that the promised prefetch tooling (announced for the Q3 runtime release) is still blocked on the model team dependency; that delay materially affected our pilot timing and pushed our go-live two weeks. Our procurement team is asking for a commercial offset to reflect the lost ramp window — they suggested a one-time service credit or a partial refund for the impacted month.

Can you advise what Redwood can do here? We were explicit in the timeline in our mutual action plan and this shift has downstream billing consequences for OmniPay.

Attachments: timeline_patch_v2.csv (internal reference)

Best,
Lexi Turner
Head of Platform Partnerships
OmniPay
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Lexi Turner <lexi@omnipay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delay on tooling integration — request for offset

Lexi —

Thanks for the note and sorry again about the hit to your timeline. I spoke with the product PM and we do have a mitigation path (prefetch in beta that will land next week) but I agree that doesn’t make up for the two-week ramp slip.

Proposed immediate remedy: a one-time account credit equal to 20% of the monthly committed spend for the affected month, conditional on OmniPay signing a short addendum that confirms the new delivery milestone and keeps the committed term intact. I’ve attached a quick calculation (partial_credit_calc.xlsx) for transparency.

I need an internal approval for that concession — looping in Marissa for commercial approval and Rishi for legal language.

Next steps I suggest:
- Marissa: can you confirm whether 20% aligns with acceptable revenue impact for this account?
- Rishi: legal language for the addendum — can you draft a short clause that ties the credit to the milestone being delivered within 30 days?
- Lexi: if that looks reasonable, I’ll have a draft addendum and a DocuSign link ready by Monday.

Appreciate the patience — we want OmniPay’s go-live to succeed.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, Lexi Turner <lexi@omnipay.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delay on tooling integration — request for offset

Olga / Lexi —

I reviewed the numbers. A 20% one-time credit on the impacted monthly committed ARR is within our tolerance for an executive-approved concession, provided we capture: (1) the milestone date, (2) a commitment to ship the specific prefetch beta within 30 days, and (3) no further commercial claims beyond the one-time credit.

Provisional sign-off from finance pending Rishi’s legal addendum and a short note from Sales Ops confirming we don’t set a precedent for rolling credits on similar pilot delays.

Vivek, flagging this for your awareness — happy to route to you for final executive sign-off if you want to increase/decrease the percentage.

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, Lexi Turner <lexi@omnipay.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delay on tooling integration — request for offset

Team / Lexi —

I put together a short addendum draft and a concise clause for inclusion in the SOW:

- One-time credit equal to 20% of the monthly committed spend for the billing month corresponding to the delayed ramp.
- Credit is payable as an account credit on the next billing cycle after Redwood ships the prefetch beta and OmniPay confirms acceptance testing (acceptance = smoke test + list of three agreed checks).
- Clause explicitly states this credit is the sole financial remedy for the delay and that OmniPay waives any further claims related to the Q3 prefetch schedule.

I attached the draft SOW addendum (omnipay_sow_addendum_draft.pdf) to this thread for review. Two small legal asks: (1) confirm the acceptance criteria are actionable, and (2) confirm OmniPay’s ProcureOps contact will sign off on the acceptance.

If Marissa and Vivek are comfortable, I’ll prep the DocuSign envelope tomorrow.

—Rishi
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, Lexi Turner <lexi@omnipay.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delay on tooling integration — request for offset

Thanks all — I reviewed the numbers and the language. Approve 20% one-time credit with the conditions spelled out by Rishi. Two notes:

1) Sales Ops — please log this as an executive concession (Deal note OP-4821) and include the credit in our renewal math.
2) Legal — ensure the addendum includes the milestone date and the acceptance tests verbatim so we have a clean trigger for the credit.

Olga — please send the DocuSign link to Lexi and copy me once executed.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
